blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 13\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic with \(a = 1 > 0\): the parabola opens upward, so it has a lowest point (a minimum) and no maximum.
We must find that minimum value and where it occurs.
Plan: complete the square to write \(f(x) = (x - h)^2 + k\); the minimum is \(k\) at \(x = h\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 13\), so \(a = 1\), \(b = 6\), \(c = 13\).
To find: the minimum (or maximum) value and the \(x\) where it occurs.
Method: completing the square. A square is never negative, so the form \((x - h)^2 + k\) shows the smallest value directly.

Add and subtract (half of 6)\(^2\)
\[f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 9 - 9 + 13\]
Why: half of the coefficient of \(x\) is \(3\) and \(3^2 = 9\). Adding 9 makes \(x^2 + 6x + 9\) a perfect square; subtracting 9 keeps the value of \(f(x)\) unchanged.

Write the perfect square and simplify
\[f(x) = (x + 3)^2 - 9 + 13\]
\[f(x) = (x + 3)^2 + 4\]
Why: \(x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2\), and \(-9 + 13 = 4\).

Read the minimum
\[(x + 3)^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow f(x) \ge 4\]
Why: \((x + 3)^2\) is smallest (zero) when \(x + 3 = 0\), i.e. \(x = -3\). Then \(f(-3) = 0 + 4 = 4\). For every other \(x\) the square is positive, so \(f(x)\) is bigger than 4. Because \(a > 0\) there is no maximum.

Check
\[f(-3) = 9 - 18 + 13 = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: putting \(x = -3\) into the original function gives the same value 4.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = x^2 + 4x\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic with \(a = 1 > 0\) (opens upward), so it has a minimum value.
There is no constant term, but the method is the same.
Plan: complete the square to get \((x - h)^2 + k\) and read the minimum \(k\) at \(x = h\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 + 4x\), so \(a = 1\), \(b = 4\), \(c = 0\).
To find: the minimum value and where it occurs.
Method: completing the square.

Add and subtract (half of 4)\(^2\)
\[f(x) = x^2 + 4x + 4 - 4\]
Why: half of 4 is 2 and \(2^2 = 4\). Adding and subtracting the same number does not change \(f(x)\).

Write the perfect square
\[f(x) = (x + 2)^2 - 4\]
Why: \(x^2 + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)^2\).

Read the minimum
\[(x + 2)^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow f(x) \ge -4\]
Why: the square is zero only when \(x = -2\); there \(f(-2) = -4\). Anywhere else the square is positive and \(f(x) > -4\). So \(-4\) is the least value.

Check
\[f(-2) = 4 - 8 = -4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the original function gives the same value at \(x = -2\).

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = -x^2 + 8x + 13\).
blocks.explanation:
Here \(a = -1 < 0\): the parabola opens downward, so it has a highest point (a maximum).
We must find the maximum value and where it occurs.
Plan: take \(-1\) common from the \(x\)-terms, complete the square inside, and write \(f(x) = -(x - h)^2 + k\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -x^2 + 8x + 13\), so \(a = -1\), \(b = 8\), \(c = 13\).
To find: the maximum value and the \(x\) where it occurs.
Method: completing the square after taking \(-1\) common, because the square must be \(x^2 + \dots\) with coefficient 1.

Take \(-1\) common from the \(x\)-terms
\[f(x) = -(x^2 - 8x) + 13\]
Why: \(-(x^2 - 8x) = -x^2 + 8x\). Inside the bracket the coefficient of \(x^2\) is now 1.

Complete the square inside the bracket
\[f(x) = -(x^2 - 8x + 16 - 16) + 13\]
Why: half of \(-8\) is \(-4\) and \((-4)^2 = 16\). We add and subtract 16 inside, so nothing changes.

Bring \(-16\) out of the bracket
\[f(x) = -(x - 4)^2 + 16 + 13\]
\[f(x) = -(x - 4)^2 + 29\]
Why: the \(-16\) inside is multiplied by the \(-1\) outside, so it comes out as \(+16\).

Read the maximum
\[-(x - 4)^2 \le 0 \Rightarrow f(x) \le 29\]
Why: \((x - 4)^2 \ge 0\), so \(-(x - 4)^2\) is never positive. It is zero at \(x = 4\), giving the largest value \(29\).

Check
\[f(4) = -16 + 32 + 13 = 29 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the original function gives 29 at \(x = 4\).

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = -x^2 - 3x - 5\).
blocks.explanation:
\(a = -1 < 0\): the parabola opens downward, so there is a maximum value.
The coefficient of \(x\) is odd, so fractions will appear; work carefully.
Plan: take \(-1\) common, complete the square with \((\tfrac{3}{2})^2 = \tfrac{9}{4}\), then read the maximum.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -x^2 - 3x - 5\), so \(a = -1\), \(b = -3\), \(c = -5\).
To find: the maximum value and where it occurs.
Method: completing the square after taking \(-1\) common.

Take \(-1\) common from the \(x\)-terms
\[f(x) = -(x^2 + 3x) - 5\]
Why: \(-(x^2 + 3x) = -x^2 - 3x\); the bracket now starts with \(x^2\).

Complete the square inside
\[f(x) = -\left(x^2 + 3x + \tfrac{9}{4} - \tfrac{9}{4}\right) - 5\]
Why: half of 3 is \(\tfrac{3}{2}\) and \((\tfrac{3}{2})^2 = \tfrac{9}{4}\).

Bring \(-\tfrac{9}{4}\) out and simplify
\[f(x) = -\left(x + \tfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 + \tfrac{9}{4} - 5\]
\[f(x) = -\left(x + \tfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 - \tfrac{11}{4}\]
Why: \(-1 \times (-\tfrac{9}{4}) = +\tfrac{9}{4}\), and \(\tfrac{9}{4} - \tfrac{20}{4} = -\tfrac{11}{4}\).

Read the maximum
\[f(x) \le -\tfrac{11}{4}\]
Why: \(-(x + \tfrac{3}{2})^2 \le 0\), and it is 0 at \(x = -\tfrac{3}{2}\). So the largest value of \(f\) is \(-\tfrac{11}{4}\). (A maximum can be negative: the whole parabola lies below the x-axis.)

Check
\[f\left(-\tfrac{3}{2}\right) = -\tfrac{9}{4} + \tfrac{9}{2} - 5\]
\[= \tfrac{-9 + 18 - 20}{4} = -\tfrac{11}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Why: the original function gives the same value.

blocks.prompt: 1 (v) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 6x - 13\).
blocks.explanation:
\(a = 3 > 0\): the parabola opens upward, so there is a minimum value.
The coefficient of \(x^2\) is 3, not 1, so we first take 3 common from the \(x\)-terms.
Plan: \(f(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x) - 13\), complete the square inside, then read the minimum.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 6x - 13\), so \(a = 3\), \(b = 6\), \(c = -13\).
To find: the minimum value and where it occurs.
Method: completing the square after taking \(a = 3\) common.

Take 3 common from the \(x\)-terms
\[f(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x) - 13\]
Why: \(3x^2 + 6x = 3(x^2 + 2x)\). Only the \(x\)-terms go inside; \(-13\) stays outside.

Complete the square inside
\[f(x) = 3(x^2 + 2x + 1 - 1) - 13\]
Why: half of 2 is 1 and \(1^2 = 1\).

Bring \(-1\) out and simplify
\[f(x) = 3(x + 1)^2 - 3 - 13\]
\[f(x) = 3(x + 1)^2 - 16\]
Why: the \(-1\) inside is multiplied by the 3 outside, giving \(-3\).

Read the minimum
\[3(x + 1)^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow f(x) \ge -16\]
Why: the square is zero at \(x = -1\), where \(f(-1) = -16\); everywhere else \(f(x) > -16\).

Check
\[f(-1) = 3 - 6 - 13 = -16 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the original function gives the same value.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Find the maximum or minimum value of the following quadratic function by completing square: \(f(x) = -2x^2 - x + 21\).
blocks.explanation:
\(a = -2 < 0\): the parabola opens downward, so there is a maximum value.
We take \(-2\) common from the \(x\)-terms; this makes the coefficient of \(x\) inside equal to \(\tfrac{1}{2}\).
Plan: \(f(x) = -2(x^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}x) + 21\), complete the square with \((\tfrac{1}{4})^2 = \tfrac{1}{16}\), then read the maximum.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -2x^2 - x + 21\), so \(a = -2\), \(b = -1\), \(c = 21\).
To find: the maximum value and where it occurs.
Method: completing the square after taking \(a = -2\) common.

Take \(-2\) common from the \(x\)-terms
\[f(x) = -2\left(x^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}x\right) + 21\]
Why: \(-2 \times \tfrac{1}{2}x = -x\), so the bracket gives back \(-2x^2 - x\).

Complete the square inside
\[f(x) = -2\left(x^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}x + \tfrac{1}{16} - \tfrac{1}{16}\right) + 21\]
Why: half of \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) is \(\tfrac{1}{4}\) and \((\tfrac{1}{4})^2 = \tfrac{1}{16}\).

Bring \(-\tfrac{1}{16}\) out and simplify
\[f(x) = -2\left(x + \tfrac{1}{4}\right)^2 + \tfrac{2}{16} + 21\]
\[f(x) = -2\left(x + \tfrac{1}{4}\right)^2 + \tfrac{169}{8}\]
Why: \(-2 \times (-\tfrac{1}{16}) = \tfrac{1}{8}\) and \(\tfrac{1}{8} + 21 = \tfrac{1 + 168}{8} = \tfrac{169}{8}\).

Read the maximum
\[f(x) \le \tfrac{169}{8}\]
Why: \(-2(x + \tfrac{1}{4})^2 \le 0\), and it is 0 at \(x = -\tfrac{1}{4}\). So the largest value is \(\tfrac{169}{8} = 21.125\).

Check
\[f\left(-\tfrac{1}{4}\right) = -\tfrac{2}{16} + \tfrac{1}{4} + 21\]
\[= -\tfrac{1}{8} + \tfrac{2}{8} + 21 = \tfrac{169}{8} \;\checkmark\]
Why: the original function gives the same value.
